_comment: The evaluation set. Two kinds of question, and BOTH are required to say
anything useful about this system.
answerable   the corpus contains the answer. `expect_sources` lists the
article title(s) that should be retrieved. Measures whether
retrieval FINDS the right evidence.
unanswerable the corpus does not cover it. The system must refuse.
Measures whether the gate actually holds.
Measuring only the first kind is the classic mistake: a system with the
similarity floor set to -1 scores 100% on answerable questions and is
completely useless, because it also answers everything else confidently
and wrongly. The two rates trade against each other, and the floor is
chosen from that trade-off rather than guessed -- see `rag eval`.
The unanswerable questions are deliberately NOT random trivia. They are
adjacent to the corpus -- same fields, same vocabulary, plausible things
to ask a system built on these articles. 'What is the capital of France?'
is easy to refuse and proves almost nothing; 'What is Postgres's default
isolation level?' is the honest test, because the corpus is full of
database talk that scores well without containing the answer.
Ground truth was established by reading the articles, not by asking the
model what it thought it knew.

unanswerable.why: The corpus discusses SQLite at length but never Postgres isolation.

unanswerable.question: What is the time complexity of quicksort?
unanswerable.why: Plain CS fundamentals; these are engineering blog posts, not textbooks.

unanswerable.question: Which company won the 2024 Formula One constructors' championship?
unanswerable.why: Wholly outside the corpus. The easy case, included as a floor.

unanswerable.question: How do I set up OAuth2 device flow authentication in Rust?
unanswerable.why: Programming vocabulary the embeddings will partly match, on a topic absent from the corpus.

unanswerable.question: What were the main causes of the 2008 financial crisis?
unanswerable.why: A serious question with an established answer, entirely outside these articles.

unanswerable.question: How much does Cloudflare charge per million Workers requests?
unanswerable.why: THE HARD ONE. Cloudflare articles are well represented and pricing language scores well, but no article states this figure. A system that answers this is fabricating from adjacent context.

unanswerable.question: What is the recommended maximum heap size for a JVM microservice?
unanswerable.why: Performance-tuning vocabulary that overlaps the SQLite and cost articles without being covered anywhere.
